evidence.detail: The class owns one R50 ParticleDefinition plus live color, size, alpha, age/dead state, world position and velocity/gravity-derived integer components, initialized directly from the definition.

Its tick method increments age, expires at ParticleDefinition lifespan, advances color/size/alpha, integrates position from velocity, advances velocity by the definition step, and applies the optional additional movement vector.

R87 GpuRenderer and R96 ModelPusher consume this class directly to emit particle geometry/color/alpha into GPU staging buffers; rs/a/h creates instances from ParticleDefinition during model particle spawning.
The state/update semantics mirror R50 Particle but this is a separate GPU-optimized runtime representation with renderer-specific fields and pooling identity.

proposals.note: GpuParticleInstance is descriptive rather than a recovered original source identifier. Exact v308 proves the live GPU particle role; confidence is 0.997.

evidence.detail: The class owns global live/recycled collections for rs/k/c/a instances, caps the live particle map at 50,000, and emits the exact diagnostic '[GPU] Reached max capacity of particle pool!' before clearing on overflow.
Allocation reuses recycled instances when available, resets their ParticleDefinition/position/model/render state, reinitializes definition-derived values, and reinserts them into the live maps/sets.
The global update loop ticks every live particle, removes expired instances from active maps, and returns them to a recycle list up to the same 50,000-instance bound.
The same manager creates/reuses up to 50 rs/k/c/d batch objects keyed by integer render/model identity and ages unused batches out after 60 seconds.

proposals.note: GpuParticlePool is descriptive exact-behavior recovery. No surviving public source identifier was found for this SpawnPK-local GPU pooling layer; confidence is 0.997.

evidence.detail: Each instance stores one integer grouping key and two primitive long-ID lists used to track active and pending-removal GPU particle instance IDs.
A batch accepts at most 1,000 particle IDs and updates its last-use timestamp on capacity checks and insertion.
Its cleanup pass resolves each particle ID through GpuParticlePool, rejects missing/wrong-key/dead-or-recycled members, removes rejected IDs, and preserves only live members matching the batch key.
R96 ModelPusher and rs/a/h obtain these keyed objects from GpuParticlePool and iterate their member particles as one renderer/model grouping.

proposals.note: GpuParticleBatch is descriptive exact-behavior recovery for the keyed 1,000-particle render grouping. No original source noun survives; confidence is 0.997.
